questions.stem: This illustration shows a proximal (type A) aortic dissection whose flap disrupts the aortic valve leaflet alignment. If this produces acute severe aortic regurgitation, what is the most immediate life-threatening consequence?

choices.text: Systemic hypertension with a widened pulse pressure over months

choices.text: Gradual, well-tolerated LV dilation over many years

choices.label: C
choices.text: Acute pulmonary edema and cardiogenic shock

questions.topicName: Aortic Regurgitation and Pulmonary Valve Disease
questions.stem: Using the Laplace relationship shown (T = P·r / 2h), what is the functional purpose of the increased wall thickness (h) that develops in concentric hypertrophy during pressure overload?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increasing wall thickness has no effect on wall tension

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increasing wall thickness reduces the intraventricular pressure directly

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increasing wall thickness enlarges the chamber radius

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increasing wall thickness raises wall tension to boost contraction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increasing wall thickness lowers wall tension back toward normal

explanation.summary: By the law of Laplace, wall tension is proportional to pressure times radius and inversely proportional to wall thickness. In pressure overload, thickening the wall (increased h) offsets the increased pressure so that tension is normalized. In volume overload, the radius rises and eccentric hypertrophy predominates.
explanation.whyCorrect: By the law of Laplace, wall tension is proportional to pressure times radius and inversely proportional to wall thickness. In pressure overload, thickening the wall (increased h) offsets the increased pressure so that tension is normalized. In volume overload, the radius rises and eccentric hypertrophy predominates.
